title: Rotate a Chain Right by K Positions
statement: You are given a list of integer values that you should treat as the payloads of a singly linked chain, where values[i] is the value of the i-th node and each node points to the next, and a non-negative integer k that may be far larger than the chain's length. Rotate the chain to the right by k positions: the last k % n elements (where n is the number of nodes) move to the front while keeping their original relative order, and everything else shifts right. Return the values of the resulting chain as a list, in head-to-tail order. If the chain is empty (n == 0) or k % n == 0, return the values unchanged. Solve it with the linked-list technique: count the length n, connect the tail back to the head to form a ring, then break the ring at the node in position n - k % n (0-indexed) to expose the new head. Example: values = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], k = 2 gives [4, 5, 1, 2, 3].
hints: If k is much larger than the chain length, how many distinct results can a right rotation actually produce? What does that tell you about k?
Reduce k modulo n first. Then note that after the rotation the new head sits at index n - (k % n), so if you close the chain into a ring you only need to find and break at that one node.

Count the length n while walking to the tail, point tail.next back at head to form a ring, advance a pointer n - k % n - 1 steps from head to land on the new tail, save new_tail.next as the new head, set new_tail.next = None, then read out the values from the new head.
